    uid=g6:5_445 StaticText " because it observes in the infrared spectrum, which has longer wavelengths than the Hubble's visible spectrum. Two concept studies were commissioned in 1999, for a potential launch in 2007 and a US$1 billion budget. The program saw enormous cost overruns and delays.       uid=g6:5_1485 StaticText "However, there is a challenge in the design of infrared telescopes: they must remain extremely cold, and the longer the wavelength of infrared light, the colder they must be. If not, the device's background heat overwhelms the detectors, effectively rendering it blind. This can be overcome by careful design. One method is to put the key instruments in a "
      uid=g6:5_1486 link "dewar" description="Cryogenic storage dewar" url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cryogenic_storage_dewar"

    uid=g6:5_2537 region "Mission goals"
      uid=g6:5_2538 heading "Mission goals" level="2"
      uid=g6:5_2539 link "edit" description="Edit section: Mission goals" url="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Webb_Space_Telescope&action=edit&section=17"
        uid=g6:5_2540 StaticText "edit"
      uid=g6:5_2541 StaticText "The James Webb Space Telescope has four key goals:"
      uid=g6:5_2542 StaticText "to search for light from the first stars and galaxies that formed in the universe after the Big Bang"
      uid=g6:5_2543 StaticText "to study "
      uid=g6:5_2544 link "galaxy formation and evolution" description="Galaxy formation and evolution" url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galaxy_formation_and_evolution"
        uid=g6:5_2545 StaticText "galaxy formation and evolution"
      uid=g6:5_2546 StaticText "to understand "
      uid=g6:5_2547 link "star formation" description="Star formation" url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_formation"

Since water vapor and carbon dioxide in Earth's atmosphere strongly absorb most infrared radiation, ground-based infrared astronomy is limited to narrow wavelength ranges where the atmosphere absorbs less strongly.     uid=g6:5_2860 region "Ground support and operations"
      uid=g6:5_2861 heading "Ground support and operations" level="2"
      uid=g6:5_2862 link "edit" description="Edit section: Ground support and operations" url="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Webb_Space_Telescope&action=edit&section=20"
        uid=g6:5_2863 StaticText "edit"
      uid=g6:5_2864 StaticText "The "
      uid=g6:5_2865 link "Space Telescope Science Institute" url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Telescope_Science_Institute"
        uid=g6:5_2866 StaticText "Space Telescope Science Institute"
      uid=g6:5_2867 StaticText " (STScI), in "
      uid=g6:5_2868 link "Baltimore, Maryland" url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltimore,_Maryland"
        uid=g6:5_2869 StaticText "Baltimore, Maryland"
      uid=g6:5_2870 StaticText ", on the "
      uid=g6:5_2871 link "Homewood Campus of Johns Hopkins University" url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homewood_Campus_of_Johns_Hopkins_University"
        uid=g6:5_2872 StaticText "Homewood Campus of Johns Hopkins University"
      uid=g6:5_2873 StaticText ", was selected in 2003 as the Science and Operations Center (S&OC) for Webb with an initial budget of US$162.2 million intended to support operations through the first year after launch."
      uid=g6:5_2874 link "[176]" url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Webb_Space_Telescope#cite_note-178"
        uid=g6:5_2875 StaticText "["
        uid=g6:5_2876 StaticText "176"
        uid=g6:5_2877 StaticText "]"
      uid=g6:5_2878 StaticText " In this capacity, STScI was to be responsible for the scientific operation of the telescope and delivery of data products to the astronomical community. Data was to be transmitted from Webb to the ground via the "
      uid=g6:5_2879 link "NASA Deep Space Network" url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA_Deep_Space_Network"
        uid=g6:5_2880 StaticText "NASA Deep Space Network"
      uid=g6:5_2881 StaticText ", processed and calibrated at STScI, and then distributed online to astronomers worldwide. As with Hubble, anyone, anywhere in the world, will be allowed to submit proposals for observations. Each year, several astronomy committees will "
      uid=g6:5_2882 link "peer review" description="Peer review" url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review"
        uid=g6:5_2883 StaticText "peer review"
      uid=g6:5_2884 StaticText " submitted proposals to select the projects to observe the following year. The authors of the selected proposals will typically have 1 year of private access to the new observations, after which the data will become publicly available for download from the STScI online archive."
      uid=g6:5_2885 link "[177]" url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Webb_Space_Telescope#cite_note-179"
        uid=g6:5_2886 StaticText "["
        uid=g6:5_2887 StaticText "177"
        uid=g6:5_2888 StaticText "]"
      uid=g6:5_2889 StaticText "The bandwidth and digital throughput of the satellite are designed to operate at 458 gigabits of data per day for the length of the mission (equivalent to a sustained rate of 5.42 "
      uid=g6:5_2890 link "Mbps" url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mbps"
        uid=g6:5_2891 StaticText "Mbps"
      uid=g6:5_2892 StaticText ")."
      uid=g6:5_2893 link "[40]" url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Webb_Space_Telescope#cite_note-wired-20191022-41"
        uid=g6:5_2894 StaticText "["
        uid=g6:5_2895 StaticText "40"
        uid=g6:5_2896 StaticText "]"
      uid=g6:5_2897 StaticText " Most of the data processing on the telescope is done by conventional single-board computers."
      uid=g6:5_2898 link "[178]" url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Webb_Space_Telescope#cite_note-180"
        uid=g6:5_2899 StaticText "["

      uid=g6:5_2903 link "Application Specific Integrated Circuit" description="Application-specific integrated circuit" url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Application-specific_integrated_circuit"
        uid=g6:5_2904 StaticText "Application Specific Integrated Circuit"
      uid=g6:5_2905 StaticText "). NASA stated that the SIDECAR ASIC will include all the functions of a "
      uid=g6:5_2906 StaticText "9.1"
      uid=g6:5_2907 StaticText " "
      uid=g6:5_2908 StaticText "kg (20"
      uid=g6:5_2909 StaticText " "
      uid=g6:5_2910 StaticText "lb)"
      uid=g6:5_2911 StaticText " instrument box in a "

      uid=g6:5_2913 StaticText " "
      uid=g6:5_2914 StaticText "cm (1.2"
      uid=g6:5_2915 StaticText " "
      uid=g6:5_2916 StaticText "in)"
      uid=g6:5_2917 StaticText " package and consume only 11"
      uid=g6:5_2918 StaticText " "
      uid=g6:5_2919 StaticText "milliwatts of power."
      uid=g6:5_2920 link "[179]" url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Webb_Space_Telescope#cite_note-Sidecar-181"
        uid=g6:5_2921 StaticText "["
        uid=g6:5_2922 StaticText "179"
        uid=g6:5_2923 StaticText "]"
      uid=g6:5_2924 StaticText " Since this conversion must be done close to the detectors, on the cold side of the telescope, the low power dissipation is crucial for maintaining the low temperature required for optimal operation of Webb."
      uid=g6:5_2925 link "[179]" url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Webb_Space_Telescope#cite_note-Sidecar-181"
        uid=g6:5_2926 StaticText "["

        uid=g6:5_2945 StaticText "The C3"

          uid=g6:5_2947 StaticText "["
          uid=g6:5_2948 StaticText "c"
          uid=g6:5_2949 StaticText "]"
        uid=g6:5_2950 StaticText " mirror segment suffered a "
        uid=g6:5_2951 link "micrometeoroid" description="Micrometeoroid" url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Micrometeoroid"
          uid=g6:5_2952 StaticText "micrometeoroid"
        uid=g6:5_2953 StaticText " strike from a large dust mote-sized particle between 23 and 25 May 2022, the fifth and largest strike since launch, reported 8 June 2022, which required engineers to compensate for the strike using a mirror actuator."
        uid=g6:5_2954 link "[182]" url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Webb_Space_Telescope#cite_note-wHarwood-185"
          uid=g6:5_2955 StaticText "["

          uid=g6:5_2957 StaticText "]"
        uid=g6:5_2958 StaticText " Despite the strike, a NASA characterization report states "all JWST observing modes have been reviewed and confirmed to be ready for science use" as of 10 July 2022."
        uid=g6:5_2959 link "[183]" url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Webb_Space_Telescope#cite_note-Howell_2022-07-18-186"
          uid=g6:5_2960 StaticText "["
          uid=g6:5_2961 StaticText "183"
          uid=g6:5_2962 StaticText "]"
        uid=g6:5_2963 StaticText " Micrometeoroids strike Webb an average of once or twice per month, and only the May 2022 strike caused noticeable damage."
        uid=g6:5_2964 link "[184]" url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Webb_Space_Telescope#cite_note-187"
          uid=g6:5_2965 StaticText "["
          uid=g6:5_2966 StaticText "184"
          uid=g6:5_2967 StaticText "]"
        uid=g6:5_2968 StaticText " After that strike, mission personnel implemented a strategy to change Webb's observations to reduce the risk of further damage. The strategy is to avoid pointing the mirror toward "micrometeoroid avoidance zones" at particular points along Webb's orbit."
        uid=g6:5_2969 link "[185]" url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Webb_Space_Telescope#cite_note-188"

        uid=g6:5_3291 StaticText "Mirror alignment requires each of the 18 mirror segments and the secondary mirror to be positioned to within 50 nanometers.         uid=g6:5_3300 link "Segment alignment begins by defocusing the segment images by moving the secondary mirror slightly. Mathematical analysis, known as phase retrieval, is applied to defocused photos to determine the precise positioning errors of the segments. Adjusting the segments then yields 18 well-corrected "telescopes". However, the segments still do not work together as a single mirror." description="Segment alignment begins by defocusing the segment images by moving the secondary mirror slightly.         uid=g6:5_3303 link "Image stacking. To put all the light in a single place, each segment image must be stacked on top of the others. This process prepares the telescope for coarse phasing." description="Image stacking. To put all the light in a single place, each segment image must be stacked on top of the others.         uid=g6:5_3322 StaticText ","
        uid=g6:5_3323 link "[222]" url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Webb_Space_Telescope#cite_note-Webb_blog_2022-01-31-225"
          uid=g6:5_3324 StaticText "["

        uid=g6:5_3328 link "NIRCam" url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NIRCam"
          uid=g6:5_3329 StaticText "NIRCam"
        uid=g6:5_3330 StaticText " targeted the 7th-magnitude star HD 84406 in "
        uid=g6:5_3331 link "Ursa Major" url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ursa_Major"
          uid=g6:5_3332 StaticText "Ursa Major"
        uid=g6:5_3333 StaticText "."
        uid=g6:5_3334 link "[d]" url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Webb_Space_Telescope#cite_note-227"
          uid=g6:5_3335 StaticText "["
          uid=g6:5_3336 StaticText "d"
          uid=g6:5_3337 StaticText "]"
        uid=g6:5_3338 link "[224]" url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Webb_Space_Telescope#cite_note-GZM-20220204-228"
          uid=g6:5_3339 StaticText "["
          uid=g6:5_3340 StaticText "224"
          uid=g6:5_3341 StaticText "]"
        uid=g6:5_3342 link "[225]" url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Webb_Space_Telescope#cite_note-FT-20220206-229"
          uid=g6:5_3343 StaticText "["
          uid=g6:5_3344 StaticText "225"
          uid=g6:5_3345 StaticText "]"
        uid=g6:5_3346 StaticText " To do this, NIRCam took 1560 images of the sky and used these wide-ranging images to determine where in the sky each segment of the main mirror initially pointed."
        uid=g6:5_3347 link "[226]" url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Webb_Space_Telescope#cite_note-Webb_blog_2022-02-11-230"
          uid=g6:5_3348 StaticText "["
          uid=g6:5_3349 StaticText "226"
          uid=g6:5_3350 StaticText "]"
        uid=g6:5_3351 StaticText " At first, the individual primary mirror segments were greatly misaligned, so the image contained 18 separate, blurry images of the star field, each containing an image of the target star. The 18 images of HD 84406 are matched to their respective mirror segments, and the 18 segments are brought into approximate alignment centered on the star ("Segment Image Identification"). Each segment was then corrected for its major focusing errors using a technique called "
        uid=g6:5_3352 link "phase retrieval" description="Phase retrieval" url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phase_retrieval"
          uid=g6:5_3353 StaticText "phase retrieval"
        uid=g6:5_3354 StaticText ", yielding 18 high-quality images from the 18 mirror segments ("Segment Alignment"). The 18 images from each segment were then moved so they precisely overlap to create a single image ("Image Stacking")."
        uid=g6:5_3355 link "[221]" url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Webb_Space_Telescope#cite_note-Webb_blog_2022-02-03-224"
          uid=g6:5_3356 StaticText "["
          uid=g6:5_3357 StaticText "221"
          uid=g6:5_3358 StaticText "]"
        uid=g6:5_3359 StaticText "With the mirrors positioned to produce almost correct images, they had to be fine-tuned to an operational accuracy of 50 nanometers, less than one "
        uid=g6:5_3360 link "wavelength" description="Wavelength" url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wavelength"
          uid=g6:5_3361 StaticText "wavelength"
        uid=g6:5_3362 StaticText " of the light that will be detected. A technique called "
        uid=g6:5_3363 StaticText "dispersed fringe sensing"
        uid=g6:5_3364 StaticText " was used to compare images from 20 pairings of mirrors, allowing most of the errors to be corrected ("Coarse Phasing"), and then introduced light defocus to each segment's image, allowing detection and correction of almost all remaining errors ("Fine Phasing"). These two processes were repeated three times, and Fine Phasing will be routinely checked throughout the telescope's operation. After three rounds of Coarse and Fine Phasing, the telescope was well aligned at a single location in the NIRCam field of view. Measurements will be made at various points in the captured image across all instruments, and corrections will be calculated from the detected intensity variations, yielding a well-aligned outcome across all instruments ("Telescope Alignment Over Instrument Fields of View"). Finally, a final round of Fine Phasing and image-quality checks on all instruments was performed to ensure that any remaining small residual errors from the previous steps were corrected ("Iterate Alignment for Final Correction"). The telescope's mirror segments were then aligned, allowing it to capture precise, focused images."
        uid=g6:5_3365 link "[221]" url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Webb_Space_Telescope#cite_note-Webb_blog_2022-02-03-224"
          uid=g6:5_3366 StaticText "["
          uid=g6:5_3367 StaticText "221"
          uid=g6:5_3368 StaticText "]"
        uid=g6:5_3369 StaticText "In preparation for alignment, NASA announced at 19:28 UTC on 3 February 2022, that NIRCam had detected the telescope's first "
        uid=g6:5_3370 link "photons" description="Photon" url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photon"
          uid=g6:5_3371 StaticText "photons"
        uid=g6:5_3372 StaticText " (although not yet complete images)."
        uid=g6:5_3373 link "[221]" url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Webb_Space_Telescope#cite_note-Webb_blog_2022-02-03-224"

    uid=g6:5_3453 region "Allocation of observation time"
      uid=g6:5_3454 heading "Allocation of observation time" level="2"
      uid=g6:5_3455 link "edit" description="Edit section: Allocation of observation time" url="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Webb_Space_Telescope&action=edit&section=26"
        uid=g6:5_3456 StaticText "edit"
      uid=g6:5_3457 StaticText "Webb observing time is allocated through a General Observers (GO) program, a Guaranteed Time Observations (GTO) program, a Director's Discretionary Early Release Science (DD-ERS) program,"
      uid=g6:5_3458 link "[235]" url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Webb_Space_Telescope#cite_note-240"
        uid=g6:5_3459 StaticText "["
        uid=g6:5_3460 StaticText "235"
        uid=g6:5_3461 StaticText "]"
      uid=g6:5_3462 StaticText " a calibration program, and a Director's Discretionary Time (DDT) program."
      uid=g6:5_3463 link "[236]" url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Webb_Space_Telescope#cite_note-241"
        uid=g6:5_3464 StaticText "["
        uid=g6:5_3465 StaticText "236"
        uid=g6:5_3466 StaticText "]"
      uid=g6:5_3467 StaticText " The GTO program provides guaranteed observing time for scientists who developed hardware and software components for the observatory. The GO program provides all astronomers the opportunity to apply for observing time and will represent the bulk of the observing time. GO programs are selected through peer review by a Time Allocation Committee (TAC), similar to the proposal review process used for the Hubble Space Telescope. The DDT program is used for time-critical observations."

      uid=g6:5_4217 link "mas" description="Minute and second of arc" url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minute_and_second_of_arc#Symbols_and_abbreviations"

"
      uid=g6:5_4225 StaticText "During commissioning, various asteroids were observed to determine the actual limitation for the speed of objects and it turned out to be 67 mas/s, which is more than twice the nominal value. Tracking at rates of 30–67 mas/s showed accuracies similar to tracking of slower targets. Thus, the telescope can observe also "
      uid=g6:5_4226 link "near-Earth asteroids" description="Near-Earth asteroids" url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Near-Earth_asteroids"

"

        uid=g6:5_4243 StaticText "FGS"
      uid=g6:5_4244 StaticText " had been gained, the tracking speed limit was finally set to 75 mas/s for routine observations. The first observation with a super-fast rate was the "

help[5]:
  Run `chrome-devtools-axi fill @g6:5_12 "text"` to fill the "Search Wikipedia" field
  Run `chrome-devtools-axi click @g6:5_6` to click the "Main menu" button
  Run `chrome-devtools-axi click @g6:5_2` to click the "Jump to content" link
  Run `chrome-devtools-axi scroll down` to scroll down
  Use `chrome-devtools-axi eval <expr>` for JS expressions. For multi-statement code, pass a function: `eval "() => { ...; return result }"`
